data.title: Meta just sparked an AI agent war Google is scrambling to win
data.description:
Silicon Valley’s two advertising giants are gearing up for a fight that could decide who controls the next major computing platform. Meta and Google are headed toward a head-on AI agent showdown, and the stakes go far beyond bragging rights. The race to build a digital assistant people actually trust has become a battle for control of how billions of people get things done online.


Meta’s Early Lead With Muse

Last month Meta’s Muse burst onto the scene, delivering the first widely adopted AI agent built for everyday users rather than tech insiders. Muse recently crossed 109 million downloads, a milestone that arrived faster than rivals managed in their own early days. The app’s early success, in both downloads and praise, hinted at a future where more people lean on digital helpers to manage their routines and knock out daily tasks.


Meta reports its quarterly results this Tuesday, and investors will be watching closely to see whether Muse’s momentum is translating into real business value.

Why Trust Still Favors Google

Even with billions of people plugged into Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, users have not historically trusted Meta the way they trust Google or Apple with sensitive tasks. Handling emails, calendars and digital wallets has never been Meta’s strong suit, and that gap could shape how quickly people warm up to Muse.

More cautious users may simply wait for early adopters to work out the bugs before trying an agent from Meta. Many would rather hold out for whatever consumer-focused option eventually comes from the iPhone maker or the company behind Gmail.

Analysts at Bank of America have flagged Google’s upcoming agent offering as a key risk facing Meta, pointing to the search giant’s proprietary models, custom silicon and massive product distribution as serious advantages. A broader Gemini 4 launch is expected to add fuel to that threat, and it could arrive at the exact moment Muse’s early buzz starts to cool.

Being first out of the gate has already won Meta public goodwill and a nice bump in its stock price. That said, moving fast has not made the threat from its rival any less serious. History in tech has shown that whoever launches second can still win if the product feels more polished, more trustworthy or simply more useful once the early hype fades.

The Advertising Business on the Line

Meta and Google together account for more than half of global digital ad revenue, which makes the rise of AI agents especially tricky for both. One of the core promises of agents is moving away from the screen-phone-app model that made mobile advertising so lucrative in the first place.

Fewer apps and webpages in daily life means less surface area for ads and fewer chances for companies to target users along the way. When an agent handles the shopping, people simply are not scrolling past all that paid marketing anymore.

Still, nobody expects Silicon Valley to let that revenue disappear without a fight. Online marketplaces have already shown that brands will pay to feature prominently inside a search or recommendation, and agents are unlikely to be any different once the format matures.

That tension puts both companies in an unusual spot. They built empires on steering attention toward ads, and now they are racing to build tools designed to pull attention away from exactly that kind of browsing.

A Shared Risk For Meta and Google

The bigger danger is that both companies could end up cannibalizing their own legacy businesses to chase the AI opportunity. That risk cuts deeper for Google, which has had to rebuild its era-defining search product from the inside out to make room for AI, while Meta’s advertising model is less tied to search clicks in the first place.

Since Muse launched, attention has turned back to Google’s search usage and growth. The company could face real challenges steering users toward agent-style tools while protecting the revenue search still generates, even as its success moving people onto AI Mode and Gemini offers some reason for optimism.

Investors on both sides will be watching for any slowdown in search click growth tied to rising agent use. Meta reports after the bell this week, and Google follows next week.

What It Means Going Forward

Beyond their own operational baggage, Meta and Google face one more shared obstacle — convincing investors that the enormous cost of building AI infrastructure is actually worth it. How each company answers that question in the months ahead could determine not just who wins the agent race, but who gets to define how people interact with technology for years to come.

data.title: Revolut says money is safe as Google Cloud outage drags on
data.description:
Why did Revolut suddenly stop working for customers across Britain? A person familiar with the matter says the bank’s outage is tied to a disruption at Google Cloud in London, where multiple services have been suffering elevated errors and intermittent network failures.


What Google has said

The disruption began shortly after 7 a.m. London time today, in the company’s europe-west2 region, which covers the London area. Google said its engineering team is investigating and apologized to those affected. In a midday update, it said the problems were continuing and advised affected customers to move their work to other locations. The cause has not been identified.


How Revolut was affected

Revolut’s status page showed most of its services were unavailable or only partly working, including card payments and ATM withdrawals. The bank said all customers’ money and data are safe. Revolut has not given a cause, and the link to Google Cloud comes from an unnamed source.

Other banks reporting problems

Reports on the outage tracker Downdetector pointed to issues at several British banks and websites starting around 7 a.m., including Lloyds and HSBC. It is not yet clear whether those outages are connected to Google.

Lloyds said customers could still log in, but some online services were not working, and it is monitoring the situation. HSBC had not responded to requests for comment. Separately, ING Germany reported trouble logging into online banking and its app because of a technical issue, though no link to Google has been confirmed.

Why a cloud outage spreads

Many companies run their apps and online services out of Google’s data centers. When a region has trouble, the businesses relying on it can be disrupted at once.

What happens next

This is a developing story. Customers are being directed to Google’s status dashboard and to each bank’s own channels for updates.

data.title: Ex-OpenAI employee’s Apple leap is under scrutiny
data.description:
OpenAI has accused a former employee who left for Apple of taking more than 100 confidential files tied to an unreleased product and presenting that material directly to senior Apple executives. The allegation appeared in a new court filing, adding fresh weight to an already high-stakes legal dispute between two of the most influential technology companies in the world.


OpenAI has raised concern that proprietary information may now be moving through Apple’s engineering teams and influencing product development from the inside.


The courtroom fallout

The filing landed in a U.S. federal court in San Jose, Calif., on Oct. 13, one day before the two companies were scheduled to face each other before a judge. That hearing was pushed back after the new allegation surfaced. OpenAI also signaled it may pursue a countersuit.

Apple denied the claims outright, saying its internal policies are built to prevent new hires from importing confidential material from previous employers. The company said it found no evidence to support OpenAI’s allegations.

OpenAI roots of the rivalry

The conflict traces back to a trade secrets lawsuit Apple filed against OpenAI earlier this year. Apple alleged that employees who moved from the iPhone maker to OpenAI’s hardware division had carried confidential information with them when they left. OpenAI denied those allegations.

U.S. District Court Judge Edward Davila later granted part of Apple’s request for expedited access to digital files. Apple was permitted to collect data from devices belonging to certain former employees and to depose three of them on an accelerated schedule. Among them are Chang Liu, a former senior system electrical engineer, and Tang Yew Tan, a former vice president of product design for the iPhone and Apple Watch.

Growing overlap

OpenAI’s latest filing arrives as Apple deepens its push into artificial intelligence and brings new products to market. OpenAI pointed to Apple’s recent HomeView launch as evidence of increasing competitive overlap between the two companies.

The case is not expected to reach trial until October 2027, though OpenAI has said it could be prepared to proceed as early as June 2027.

data.title: 7 warning signs a text message is a scam and what to do next
data.description:
Text scams are now the most common way fraudsters first reach Americans. In March, the Federal Trade Commission told Congress that a text message was the top contact method in fraud reports for 2025, a year when people reported a record $15.9 billion in total fraud losses. The best protection is simple. Don’t click links or reply to texts you weren’t expecting. If a message seems real, contact the company yourself using a number or website you already trust.


That advice matters more than ever, because the old tells are fading. Artificial intelligence now helps scammers write clean, polished messages that sound like your bank, the post office or your boss. The typos you used to look for may not be there.


How big is the text scam problem?

It’s growing fast. In 2024, Americans reported losing $470 million to scams that began with a text, five times more than in 2020, according to the FTC. The share of text scam reports that involved lost money climbed from 5% in 2020 to 11% in 2024. The FTC says reported losses are only a fraction of the real total, because many victims never report.

Researchers at the fraud prevention company Sift found that scams they identified as using AI rose 456% between May 2024 and April 2025, Forbes reported. Text messages also get opened at rates as high as 98%, according to FTC materials, which makes them an easy target.

What are the most common text scams right now?

The FTC found that five schemes made up about half of all text fraud reports in 2024. Fake package delivery problems topped the list, followed by fake job offers, fake bank fraud alerts, unpaid toll notices and texts that pretend to be sent to the wrong number. That last one often turns into a long, friendly conversation that ends with a pitch for a fake investment.

The job version, often called a task scam, pays you small amounts at first for easy work like rating products. Then it asks you to deposit your own money to unlock bigger earnings, and the money disappears. Other common tricks include fake IRS or Social Security notices, fake prize offers, fake tech support warnings and messages asking you to share a verification code someone just sent you.

Expect scammers to borrow from the headlines. With the 2027 Social Security increase just announced, the midterm elections weeks away and holiday shopping starting, fake benefit notices, election messages and delivery alerts are likely to pick up.

What are the red flags of a scam text?

Pressure is the biggest one. Scam texts push you to act now to avoid a fine, a frozen account or a lost package. Real banks and government agencies don’t threaten you by text. Be suspicious of any link in a text you didn’t expect, especially shortened links or web addresses that almost match a real brand.

No legitimate company will ask you for your Social Security number, password, PIN or card details by text. Requests to pay with gift cards, crypto or a payment app are another warning sign. A generic greeting can be a clue, but scammers now pull names from data breaches, so a text that uses your name isn’t automatically safe. The sender’s number alone won’t tell you much either, since scammers can fake numbers, including ones that look like your bank’s.

What should you do if you clicked a scam text?

Act fast. Stop replying and block the number. If you shared card or bank details, call your bank using the number on the back of your card and ask it to freeze the account. If you gave out your Social Security number, go to IdentityTheft.gov and place a fraud alert or credit freeze with Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. If you paid with a gift card, call the card company right away and keep your receipts. Change any passwords that may be exposed and turn on two step login.

Then report it. Forward the text to 7726, which spells SPAM, so your carrier can block similar messages, and file a report at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

How can you block text scams before they reach you?

Turn on your phone’s spam filter. On iPhone, look for the option to screen or filter unknown senders in your Messages settings. On Android, open Google Messages settings and enable spam protection. Major carriers offer free blocking tools, and apps like Nomorobo and Hiya add another layer. Don’t reply to suspicious texts, even to type STOP, because a reply confirms your number is active.

For many families, the most powerful protection is a phone call. Check in with older relatives, share these red flags and agree on one rule. When in doubt, don’t click.

data.title: GTA 6 leaker abruptly quits after his crypto coin crashes
data.description:
The hacker behind a wave of Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks says he’s calling it quits, and it seems gamers had a lot to do with it.


Cyberleek, the leaker who has been posting content from an illegally obtained playable version of the highly anticipated game, announced Wednesday, Oct. 14, that his leaks are ending. The decision came after the cryptocurrency coin he tied to his releases plummeted in value, according to Forbes.


How the leaks were tied to a crypto coin

Cyberleek recently resurfaced after a break of about a month and a half. Rather than simply posting new material, he linked each release to his crypto coin’s market cap, promising specific clips once the coin hit certain dollar goals.

About a week ago, after the market cap passed $5 million, he released explicit footage showing the game’s lead characters, Jason and Lucia, without clothing.

He then unveiled a new leak roadmap. Under the plan, footage of tanks and fighter jets would arrive once the coin reached $10 million, $15 million and $20 million. The biggest threat came at the top of the list, as Cyberleek claimed he would release the full 200 GB build of the game if the market cap hit $30 million.

Gamers refused to play along

Players didn’t take the bait. Instead of pumping money into the coin to unlock more leaks, they let it slide. The coin’s market cap dropped to about $1.26 million, far below any of the targets on his roadmap.

Many fans appeared more interested in experiencing the game for themselves when it launches than in seeing it spoiled early.

Inside Cyberleek’s goodbye message

On Wednesday morning, Cyberleek posted a lengthy statement on his website announcing that the leaks were over. Roughly half of the message focused on the coin, as he tried to explain that he wasn’t motivated by greed and wasn’t attempting a rug pull, a scam in which crypto creators abandon a project after collecting investors’ money.

The rest of the message addressed what might happen next. Cyberleek claimed he has a so-called dead man’s switch that would release story spoilers if he were caught. He also said he had intentionally avoided posting plot details to avoid ruining the experience for players, and suggested that Rockstar’s parent company, Take-Two Interactive, had already been punished enough.

He said the leaks were finished for now, leaving the door open to a possible return.

A crusade that fell flat

Cyberleek had framed his actions as a stand for consumers, criticizing Rockstar over its decision not to produce physical discs for the game. But tying the leaks to a crypto coin that could directly profit him raised doubts about those claims.

The leaks also lost much of their impact over time. Rockstar began sharing more of its own high-quality footage and details about the game, giving fans an official look at what’s coming and making the unauthorized clips feel far less important. For most players, the official material offered a better way to preview the game.

Rockstar’s investigation continues

Even if Cyberleek has stopped posting, the story is far from over. The breach remains a serious security issue for Rockstar, which is expected to continue investigating how the build got out and working to identify the person responsible.

It isn’t the first time the studio has dealt with a major leak. In 2022, early development footage of the game spread online after a hack, long before Rockstar officially revealed the title.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is set to launch Nov. 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, just over a month away. With release day approaching, many fans are simply counting down the days until they can explore the game legitimately.

This story was originally reported by Forbes.

data.title: Anthropic launches Claude Duet: An always-on AI agent for your workday
data.description:
Anthropic has launched Claude Duet, an AI agent built to handle busywork for professionals and small business owners. Announced today, Oct. 21, the research preview runs as its own app on iOS, Android and the web, and it is opening first to Claude Pro and Max subscribers in the United States through a waitlist.


Duet is Anthropic’s answer to Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots in a growing race to build personal agents that are always on. Unlike a chatbot that waits for questions, Duet watches a user’s connected apps, sends a short brief each morning and sends a message only when something needs attention.


What can Claude Duet do?

Users can hand Duet tasks ranging from scheduling meetings to building dashboards, drafting financial or sales forecasts, and prototyping web apps. It runs on Claude Opus 5.5, the model Anthropic released in late September.

Duet works on its own cloud computer with a browser, so it keeps going after the user closes the app. It also carries over a user’s memory, skills and connected apps from their Claude account, which keeps setup short.

We’re opening a research preview of Claude Duet, a new app where Claude works as a proactive agent.

It comes to you with what needs your attention, completes tasks you ask of it, keeps working when you step away, and checks with you before it acts on your behalf. https://t.co/kt8gAbWuX8

— Claude (@claudeai) October 21, 2026

Is Claude Duet safe to use with sensitive information?

Anthropic says Duet asks for approval before big steps such as sending a payment or deleting something. The company also released a new classifier and safety system prompt that check each message. They are designed to block the most sensitive information, such as credit card numbers and government ID numbers. Health and personal financial details pass only when a user specifically tells Duet to send them.

Anthropic says Duet never directly sees passwords or sign-in tokens. The company says internal red teams and an outside firm tested it for security weaknesses, and it is covered by Anthropic’s public bug bounty program.

What are Claude Duet’s limits?

Anthropic calls Duet an early version. The company says it might misread a thread or misjudge what is urgent, and it is not yet as strong at personal errands like booking tickets.

During the preview, Duet draws from the same usage limits as the rest of a subscriber’s Claude plan. Anthropic has not announced separate pricing. Access for Team and Enterprise plans is expected later.

Why is Claude Duet aimed at small business owners?

Duet’s development was led by Karan Ahuja, who ran product management at Meta Superintelligence Labs until July before joining Anthropic in August. He said the team built it for professionals and small business owners juggling a lot at work and at home.

That pitch lands with a lot of people. In communities where so many entrepreneurs wear every hat at once, from the salon owner answering clients between appointments to the side hustler running a brand from a phone, an assistant that sorts priorities and drafts the forecast is a real offer.

How does Claude Duet compare with Meta’s Muse?

Muse has a big head start. Data firm Apptopia estimates Muse had passed 14 million installs as of today. Anthropic announced Duet on the same day Meta reported earnings, and Meta Superintelligence Labs chief Alexandr Wang responded with a meme about how much Duet resembles Muse. Meta also recently paused a Muse sharing feature after researchers found users’ AI chats on the web, a reminder that privacy will shape this race as much as features.

When can you get Claude Duet?

For now, only through the waitlist. Anthropic says it will email users when their access is ready, and Ahuja said the company is letting people in as quickly as possible.

The launch comes as Anthropic approaches an IPO that Business Insider reports could value the company at as much as $2 trillion. The agent is ready to work. The bigger question is how many people are ready to hand it the keys.

data.title: Apple Music changed something after 11 years and fans are furious
data.description:
Apple rarely touches the identity of its biggest apps, which is exactly why this latest move caught so many people off guard. After 11 years with essentially the same look, Apple Music is getting its first real redesign, and the reaction online has been anything but quiet.


The change was quietly spotted buried inside a handful of developer betas, long before any formal announcement, which only added to the sense that something significant was being tested without the usual fanfare.


What Apple Actually Changed

The update starts with the wordmark itself. The tech giant swapped the familiar capitalized Music text for an entirely lowercase version in a much thicker, bolder typeface, giving the logo a wider, heavier feel compared to the slim lettering fans have scrolled past for over a decade. The new look first appeared alongside Apple Music Hall, the company’s new performance venue at London’s Battersea Power Station, before showing up inside developer betas for iOS and macOS.

That alone might have passed as a one-off venue branding choice. Instead, the redesign went further, with Apple testing an entirely new app icon that replaces the signature red background behind the beamed eighth symbol with a stripped-down black-and-white design. A reversed white-on-black version appears automatically in dark mode, and the company has also prepared a tintable clear version that can take on different colors depending on a person’s home screen setup.

Some early testers even noticed the change extending beyond the icon itself, with the red accent color inside the app itself swapped out for a cooler blue tone across menus and buttons, suggesting the redesign runs deeper than a simple logo swap.

Why Fans Are Furious Over the Redesign

Reaction across social media has been loud, and most of it has not been kind. Commenters have called the new icon boring and generic, with some joking that it looks like a design school assignment rather than a finished product from one of the world’s most valuable companies. A handful of people pointed out that the black-and-white treatment does resemble traditional sheet music, offering a rare bit of praise in an otherwise rough reception.

Part of the frustration seems tied to just how recognizable the old red icon had become. Apple Music’s red beamed eighth symbol sat untouched on millions of phones since the service launched, and visual habits like that are notoriously hard to let go of, even when a redesign is objectively cleaner or more modern.

A Pattern of Backlash Whenever Apple Touches an Icon

This is not the first time the company has stirred up this kind of reaction. Apple has a long history of frustrating users whenever it tweaks a familiar icon or interface, only for people to eventually adjust and, in many cases, come to prefer the new look within a year or two. The same pattern played out when the Photos app and Podcasts icons were last overhauled, each time drawing complaints that faded within a few months.

The tech industry is far from alone here either. Instagram faced a similar wave of criticism after changing its own wordmark font recently, and even a rival search giant’s subtle logo tweak a little over a year ago sparked its share of commentary, despite being barely noticeable to casual users. Redesigns at this scale almost always generate noise before they generate acceptance.

What Comes Next for Apple Music

For now, the redesigned wordmark and icon remain confined to developer betas, meaning most listeners have not seen the change firsthand yet. The public website and web player still display the original branding as of this writing.

That is expected to shift soon. The new look is tied to the rollout of iOS and macOS software updates later this month, timed close to the launch of the newest iPhone. Once those updates reach the public, the updated wordmark and icon should appear across the Apple Music app, its website and any related marketing materials, giving millions of listeners their first real look at the full redesign all at once.

Whether the backlash cools down once the design reaches everyone’s home screen, or whether Apple ends up tweaking the icon again before a full launch, remains to be seen. What is clear is that after more than a decade of staying mostly the same, Apple Music’s identity is finally catching up with the rest of Apple’s evolving design language.

data.title: What we know about the leaked Shrek 2 Remastered game
data.description:
What do we know about Shrek 2 Remastered? A listing for the game appeared early on the Xbox store today, and it revealed that publisher Aspyr is bringing the 2004 action-adventure back with a visual overhaul. The page was later taken down.


What the leak revealed

The listing included screenshots, a pre-order trailer and a full description, but no release date. The game is expected to be announced at the ID@Xbox Showcase on Tuesday, Oct. 20, at 10 a.m. PT. News of the remaster first surfaced in September, when a batch of Steam achievements leaked.


The 5 new features

The remaster promises the following upgrades.

  1. Improved graphics, with rebuilt textures, an enhanced interface, 4K resolution and cutscenes.
  2. A new Photo Mode for capturing snapshots.
  3. A Cheat Mode that lets players unlock cheats for a smoother playthrough.
  4. Co-op for up to four players, with couch, online or mixed play.
  5. The ability to swap heroes at any time to fight enemies, beat bosses and solve puzzles with each character’s unique abilities.

About the original game

Shrek 2 first launched in 2004 and was published by Activision. It loosely follows the movie’s story, with Shrek and Fiona heading to meet the in-laws, and adds sections that go beyond the film. Players move through eleven levels as one of four characters, with goals such as guiding the three blind mice home and mini-games that include punching chickens. Reviews landed in the mid-70s, and the game shipped more than five million copies.

Will it come to Nintendo consoles?

The listing does not confirm platforms. Aspyr usually releases games on multiple platforms, so a Switch 2 and Switch version seems likely, but nothing has been announced. The remaster would also arrive ahead of Shrek 5 next year.

data.title: PlayStation Plus Drops 9 October Games, One Shockingly Familiar
data.description:
A day-one debut, a returning open-world hit and a Capcom throwback lead a staggered spooky-season lineup for Extra and Premium members


October is shaping up to be a crowded month for PlayStation Plus subscribers who pay for more than the basics. Sony has revealed its Extra and Premium lineup, adding nine titles to the service over the coming weeks. The batch mixes fresh releases, a rare day-one debut and a returning blockbuster that longtime members will likely recognize.


The reveal follows the Essential tier’s monthly offering, which already gave subscribers Hunt: Showdown 1896, F1 2025 and Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2. Members on the two higher tiers now get a much deeper bench to work through as the nights grow longer.

A Staggered Rollout Continues

For years, Sony released its monthly catalog additions all on the same day. That habit has faded. The company has been testing a staggered schedule in recent months and is sticking with it for October. According to the PlayStation Blog, the first title arrived Oct. 14, and the rest will land in waves through the end of the month.

Here is the full lineup and when each game arrives:

PS Plus Game Catalog

  • The Midnight Walk (PS5) – Oct. 14
  • Mafia: The Old Country (PS5) – Oct. 20
  • Horizon Forbidden West (PS5, PS4) – Oct. 20
  • Mycopunk (PS5) – Oct. 20
  • Poppy Playtime: Chapter 2 (PS5, PS4) – Oct. 27
  • Tales of Arise – Beyond the Dawn Edition (PS5, PS4) – Oct. 27
  • Monster Energy Supercross 25 – The Official Video Game (PS5, PS4) – Oct. 27

PS Plus Classics

  • Dino Crisis 2 (PS5, PS4) – Oct. 20
  • RollerCoaster Tycoon 3 Complete Edition (PS5, PS4) – Oct. 20

PlayStation Brings Back a Familiar Favorite

Two of these additions are not exactly surprises. Sony confirmed both Mycopunk and Dino Crisis 2 during its September State of Play showcase. As always, everything in the Classics section is reserved for Premium members only.

Mycopunk stands out for another reason. It is one of the few games to launch directly on PlayStation Plus on day one, a move the service rarely makes. Subscribers get to try it without paying anything beyond their membership.

Fans of Dino Crisis 2 should keep their expectations in check when it comes to trophies. None of the Capcom classics currently on the service include them, and this one is not expected to break the pattern. It does, however, come with save states and a rewind feature, which should make the survival horror throwback far more forgiving than it was in its original form.

Then there is Horizon Forbidden West. Anyone feeling a strange sense of déjà vu is not imagining things. The open-world adventure was part of the catalog before Sony pulled it in 2024. Its return gives newer subscribers a chance to explore Aloy’s journey and offers returning players a reason to finish what they started.

Extra Perks and What Comes Next

The catalog is only part of the story. Sony is also tossing in several bonuses for subscribers this month.

Premium members can try Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy and Mortal Shell 2 starting Oct. 20. Sony has not said how long the trials will last, but any progress carries over to the full games for players who decide to buy.

Back 4 Blood, which is already in the catalog, gets a seasonal boost on Oct. 21. Extra and Premium subscribers will be able to grab the Tunnel of Terror expansion at no extra cost, while the game’s other expansions will be marked down by 95%.

Dead by Daylight players have a reason to team up, too. If the community collectively logs 10 million matches between Oct. 20 and Oct. 26, everyone unlocks a charm and a costume.

Movie fans are not left out. The Until Dawn film will be discounted for PlayStation Plus members for a limited time starting Oct. 28, though Sony has not revealed how steep the price cut will be.

With October fully mapped out, attention now shifts to November. Unless a delay or special event shakes up the schedule, the Essential lineup for next month should be announced Wednesday, Oct. 28.

Source: Comic Book

data.title: Amazon’s AI wearables listen all day: Would you wear one?
data.description:
Amazon launched two AI wearables today, that the company says can listen to conversations, compose notes and issue reminders. The first, the Bee Frontier, is a silicone wristband that can also clip to clothing and costs $74.99. The second, the Bee Eclipse, is a credit card-sized device that attaches magnetically to the back of a phone and sells for $99.99. Both are built by Bee, an AI wearable maker Amazon acquired last year.


What the devices do

Equipped with microphones, the devices transcribe meetings or everyday conversations so people can document moments hands-free. They then suggest personalized goals and actions based on what was said, according to Amazon. If someone plans a vacation on a phone call, the company says the device can summarize the trip, including flight times and hotel reservations.


Amazon also says users can connect Bee to Gmail, Google Calendar and Microsoft Outlook. The AI can then draft follow-up emails or create calendar invites based on the conversation. The devices can also link to Alexa+ and Amazon.com.

What it costs

Basic features are free. Users get conversation summaries, recaps and 14 days of memory at no charge. Advanced features, including Alexa+ and Amazon.com integration and suggested to-dos, require a Bee Pro subscription at $11.99 per month.

The privacy question

Always-listening devices raise obvious concerns, and Amazon addressed them directly. The company said no one, including Amazon, can access your data. According to the company, audio recordings are deleted after the devices transcribe them, and no one can access the data unless the user shares it. These are Amazon’s own claims, and independent verification is not part of the announcement.

A crowded market

Bee is part of a growing field of consumer AI gadgets. A news report described the category as a trillion-dollar market. Meta recently announced Muse, a pocket-sized AI assistant in the form of a keychain. Microsoft, OpenAI and Samsung have also introduced AI-powered products aimed at consumers.

Whether people will wear a device that records their conversations, and whether the privacy promises hold up over time, will likely determine how far this category goes.
